title: Myanmar-Thailand Earthquake: Salesian Missions Launches Emergency Appeal
text:
A devastating earthquake has struck Myanmar, leaving a path of destruction and a desperate need for aid. This article explores the response of Salesian Missions as they work tirelessly to provide relief and support to those affected by the Myanmar earthquake . Discover how the Salesian community is offering hope and healing in the face of this immense tragedy.
Devastating Earthquake Rocks Myanmar: Salesian Missions Respond New Rochelle, N.Y. — April 2, 2025
The Disaster Unfolds A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck Mandalay , Myanmar, on March 28, sending shockwaves across Southeast Asia. The quake’s impact reached as far as Bangkok, Thailand, where a skyscraper under construction was leveled. initial reports from the military government indicate a staggering loss of life, with over 2,000 fatalities and 3,000 injuries.However, the true extent of the devastation remains uncertain due to communication challenges within Myanmar.
Mandalay City bore the brunt of the earthquake, with widespread destruction reported. Numerous high-rise buildings, pagodas, mosques, and churches have been reduced to rubble. The iconic Sagaing Bridge, a vital artery spanning the Irrawaddy River, suffered critical damage, with sections collapsing into the water.
Salesian Response: A beacon of Hope salesian Missions, the U.S. growth arm of the Salesians of Don Bosco, has launched an emergency appeal to provide critical aid to those affected. The association is working in tandem with the global Salesian community to deliver assistance on the ground and raise essential funding.
Impact on Salesian communities Mandalay: The Salesian community endured notable damage. The St. John Paul II Chapel suffered extensive damage, including the collapse of its façade and parts of its walls.Tragically,two worshipers and a young boy were injured. The building housing street children also sustained considerable damage, affecting the ceiling, walls, and dormitory. Classrooms and the refectory were also impacted. Anisakan: Buildings housing salesian missionaries and Daughters of Mary help of Christians experienced widespread structural damage. The St. Joseph Chapel in the Provincial House community showed cracks near the altar, and the statue of st. Joseph was broken. The Salesian community in Mandalay was severely affected by the earthquake. The St. John Paul II Chapel suffered extensive damage, with its façade and parts of the walls collapsing. Tragically, two faithful who were present for Adoration were injured as well as a young boy. the building housing street children also sustained significant damage, including to its ceiling, sections of the walls and the dormitory. Classrooms and the refectory also sustained damage. The confreres’ quarters had falling plaster in several of the rooms and the corridor leading to the dining room was damaged. We will continue to assess the situation in Salesian centers and within the community.
A Salesian on the ground in Mandalay
Leadership & Solidarity Father Fabio Attard, the newly appointed Salesian Rector Major, addressed the earthquake during a Chapter Assembly in Turin. He led the assembly in prayer and invited Father Bosco Zeya aung, provincial of Myanmar, to provide an update on the situation. Fr. Attard pledged immediate Salesian support for relief efforts.
Challenges and Commitment Father Michael Conway, director of Salesian Missions, highlighted the complexities of providing aid amidst political instability in Myanmar. This earthquake is coming at a time of great political instability in Myanmar, making humanitarian aid, transportation and communication extremely challenging, he stated. Despite these obstacles, The Salesian communities, along with the local population, are struggling to respond to the urgent needs of those affected. Salesians though live where they work and know the communities and how to get things done. This perfectly positions them to respond in the immediate aftermath of a tragedy such as this and in the long-term rebuilding process.
Salesian communities remain dedicated to serving the most vulnerable, offering hope and healing despite the ongoing crisis.
How to Help To contribute to the Myanmar Earthquake Fund and support the Salesian Missions’ relief efforts,visit https://salesianmissions.org/myanmar-earthquake/ .
*Any goods, services, or funds provided by Salesian missions to programs located in this country were administered in compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including sanctions administered by the U.S. Department of Treasury’s office of Foreign Asset Control.
About Salesian Missions Salesian Missions, headquartered in New Rochelle, N.Y., is part of the Don Bosco Network, a global federation of Salesian NGOs. The organization raises funds for international programs serving youth and families in impoverished communities across more than 130 countries. Salesian missionaries provide services to children irrespective of race or religion, focusing on helping young people become self-sufficient through vocational training. To date, Salesian Missions has supported over 3 million youth.
